commit b6715ef5dace6709aeca0b69ca333a3f5395221c
Author:     John Bieling <john@thunderbird.net>
AuthorDate: Wed Jun 3 12:33:18 2026 +0300
Commit:     John Bieling <john@thunderbird.net>
CommitDate: Wed Jun 3 12:33:18 2026 +0300

    Bug 2043830 - Don't index currentAttachments by a DOM index. r=aleca
    
    The upcoming messageDisplay API for accessing and manipulating the attachments
    of the currently displayed message is heavily based on the Attachment Experiment
    we wrote a few years ago for the LookOut Add-on, whose implementation we have
    since hardened based on user feedback. One surfaced issue, however, needs to be
    fixed in Thunderbird first.
    
    https://github.com/TB-throwback/LookOut-fix-version/issues/130
    
    The API will add, remove and restore the displayed attachments by mutating
    about:message's `currentAttachments` array and rebuilding the `attachmentList`
    widget. However, `updateAttachmentsDisplay()` indexes the wrong list. It takes an
    index from the `attachmentList` widget via `attachmentList.getIndexOfItem()`, an
    index into that DOM list, and uses it to index the `currentAttachments` array:
    
        currentAttachments[index].size = attachmentInfo.size;
    
    The DOM `attachmentList` and the `currentAttachments` array are two separate
    lists that are normally kept in lockstep. They are rebuilt asynchronously,
    however: `displayAttachmentsForExpandedView()` awaits `AttachmentInfo.isEmpty()`
    for each detached or link attachment, and the completion of `isEmpty()`'s fetch
    calls back into `updateAttachmentsDisplay()`. While `currentAttachments` is being
    mutated - or while such a rebuild overlaps the native, un-awaited initial build -
    the two lists momentarily diverge. The DOM-list index can then point past the end
    of the `currentAttachments` array, and the assignment throws
    "currentAttachments[index] is undefined".
    
    The important part, however, is that the assignment is redundant: `attachmentInfo`
    is the very object stored in `currentAttachments`, and `AttachmentInfo.isEmpty()`
    has already set its `size` before invoking the callback. The line therefore only
    ever assigns an object's size to itself, except when the DOM-list index no longer
    maps to an array entry, where it throws instead.
    
    This patch removes the offending line and documents that
    `updateAttachmentsDisplay()` must operate on `attachmentInfo` only, never on
    `currentAttachments` indexed by a DOM-list index.
    
    Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D303692

diff --git a/mail/base/content/msgHdrView.js b/mail/base/content/msgHdrView.js
index 914aa60e641..c565a268c9f 100644
--- a/mail/base/content/msgHdrView.js
+++ b/mail/base/content/msgHdrView.js
@@ -2083,6 +2083,13 @@ function updateSaveAllAttachmentsButton() {
  * Update the attachments display info after a particular attachment's
  * existence has been verified.
  *
+ * Note: this function must not modify `currentAttachments[index]`. The `index`
+ * returned by `attachmentList.getIndexOfItem()` is an index into the DOM
+ * attachment list, not into the `currentAttachments` array. The two are rebuilt
+ * asynchronously and may transiently be out of sync, so indexing
+ * `currentAttachments` by it is unsafe (it can point past the end and throw).
+ * Instead, operate on `attachmentInfo` only.
+ *
  * @param {AttachmentInfo} attachmentInfo
  * @param {boolean} isFetching
  */
@@ -2119,7 +2126,6 @@ function updateAttachmentsDisplay(attachmentInfo, isFetching) {
       return;
     }
 
-    currentAttachments[index].size = attachmentInfo.size;
     const tooltiptextExternalNotFound = attachmentName.getAttribute(
       "tooltiptextexternalnotfound"
     );
